pl-l4d19c1-d1e115.summary: Having shown what the apostolic keys are and their use, turns to when and to whom they are given.

pl-l4d19c1-d1e118.summary: States that the keys are given through the bishop's ministry at promotion to the priesthood: when one receives priestly order, he receives these keys.
claims: The keys are given at priestly ordination.

pl-l4d19c1-d1e121.summary: Objects that not all, nor only, priests seem to have the keys, since many have knowledge of discernment before ordination and many lack it after.

pl-l4d19c1-d1e125.summary: Answers that not all priests have the key of discernment, which is lamentable: many without discretion and knowledge presume to take the priesthood, unworthy in life and knowledge, and never receive that key. Those who had discernment before priesthood did not have it as a key, since they could not open or close with it; at ordination they rightly receive the key of discernment, as their discretion is increased and becomes a key they can use.
claims: Not all priests have the key of knowledge.
Prior knowledge becomes a key at ordination.

pl-l4d19c1-d1e128.summary: Asks, since not all priests have both keys, whether all have the other, the power of binding and loosing.

pl-l4d19c1-d1e131.summary: Reports some who think this power was granted only to those who keep both the doctrine and life of the apostles, the keys being promised to Peter and his imitators only, and who cite authorities.
claims: Some hold that only priests of apostolic life have the power.

pl-l4d19c1-d1e134.summary: Gives their reading of Augustine: God forgives sins by himself or through the members of the dove; and sins are forgiven or retained by the saints.

pl-l4d19c1-d1e143.summary: Adds Augustine on Exodus: the golden plate on the priest's forehead signifies confidence of good life, and only the priest who has it truly and perfectly, not in sign but in reality, can take away sins.

pl-l4d19c1-d1e154.summary: Adds Gregory: only those in this flesh who hold the apostles' example together with their doctrine have the power of binding and loosing.

pl-l4d19c1-d1e164.summary: Adds Origen: this power was granted only to Peter and his imitators; whoever follows Peter's footsteps rightly has the power of binding and loosing.

pl-l4d19c1-d1e170.summary: Notes that on these texts they assert that the power was granted only to priests of apostolic life and doctrine.

pl-l4d19c1-d1e173.summary: Gives the view Lombard confesses he prefers: this key is given to all priests, but only those who keep apostolic life and doctrine have it rightly and worthily. The authorities do not deny that bad priests have the power, but mean that only imitators of the apostles use it worthily; remission and retention are done worthily only by God or the saints in whom the Spirit dwells, yet they are done through those who are not holy, though not worthily, since God gives blessing to one who asks worthily even through an unworthy minister.
claims: All priests have the power of binding and loosing.
Only priests of apostolic life use it worthily.
God blesses the worthy even through unworthy ministers.

pl-l4d19c1-d1e176.summary: Cites Jerome on 'I will give you the keys': the other apostles have the same judicial power, and the whole Church has it in bishops and presbyters; Peter received it specially so that all understand that whoever separates from the unity of faith and the Church can neither be loosed from sins nor enter heaven.
claims: All bishops and priests have the power of the keys.
Those separated from the Church cannot be loosed.

pl-l4d19c1.summary: Asks when and to whom the keys are given: through the bishop's ministry at priestly ordination. Not all priests have the key of discernment, since many unlearned are ordained, and those learned before ordination receive it as a key only then. On the power of binding and loosing, some hold only priests who keep the apostles' life and doctrine have it, citing Augustine, Gregory, and Origen. Lombard holds that all priests receive this key, but only those who keep apostolic life and doctrine use it worthily and rightly; through unworthy ministers it is done, but not worthily, since God blesses the worthy even through an unworthy minister. Jerome confirms that all bishops and priests have it, Peter receiving it specially to show that those separated from the Church cannot be loosed.
claims: The keys are given at priestly ordination.
Not all priests have the key of knowledge.
All priests have the power of binding and loosing.
Only those of apostolic life and doctrine use it worthily.
Those separated from the Church cannot be loosed.
